channel.title: Wire — Frontend
channel.description: Frontend from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: European Commission Declares Browser Competition a Digital Markets Act Priority
item.description: In comments to Politico regarding our open letter, the European Commission acknowledged the letter and noted that browsers are “effectively the entry point to… (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Mozilla Partners with Mistral to Bring Open-Weight AI Models to Firefox Smart Window
item.description: Mozilla has partnered with Mistral AI to offer Mistral Small 4, an open-weight model, in Firefox's Smart Window AI assistant, now in beta. It is recommended for users in France, the US and Canada. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Beyond 12 Columns: Designing Layouts With Personality
item.description: Too many websites look alike. They use familiar layouts, repeat the same patterns, and often leave little impression once you’ve moved on. (1 source: frontendfocus)

item.title: The Compacting Sidebar Blues
item.description: You've got a sidebar nav for a web app with icons and text. What happens where vertical space is constrained? Remove the text? But when and how? (1 source: frontendfocus)

item.title: Has the Web Stopped Getting Heavier?
item.description: In April, Ethan Gardner showed that web pages started gaining JavaScript almost three times faster after November 2022. We extended his analysis by eight months. (1 source: frontendfocus)

item.title: A New Set of HTML Insertion and Streaming APIs
item.description: Chrome is introducing a new set of HTML insertion and streaming methods that provide a more descriptive way to insert HTML into an existing element, along with the ability to stream content directly into the DOM. (1 source: frontendfocus)

item.title: AI Sped Up The Build: How Can Accessibility Testing Keep Up?
item.description: AI has sped up how teams design and build, but quality assurance (QA) testing hasn’t kept pace, and the web may be getting less accessible. (1 source: frontendfocus)
